name: sched-write-expected-goal
replace:
expectedGoalId: func() *string { _ = id; return nil }(),
		mutate:         change,
reason: apply() compares expectedGoalId with the focused goal read an instant earlier under the same lock; reconcileFocused either keeps the same focused id or fails the apply earlier, so the guard can never fire

name: sched-signal-inrun
reason: schedule() itself begins with `if s.inRun { return }`, so the caller's `!s.inRun` test is redundant

name: sched-datepars-hour
reason: an hour of 25..99 is normalized into the next day by time.Date, so the following `t.Day() != day` check already returns NaN for every input the removed test rejects

name: core-load-complete
reason: the pool read (directory scan and snapshot paths in storage.go) already drops status=complete goals, and the legacy goal added by resolveSessionFocus is never complete, so loadState's pool never holds one to delete

name: lr-anchor-fp
reason: a retained tail's anchorFingerprint is the fingerprint of base[anchorIndex-1] when it was anchored, and every apply resets unless the whole preceding history still matches baseFingerprints, so the re-check cannot differ (fingerprintMessage never returns nil in Go)

name: activity-indexed-break
reason: limit>0 and len>limit only collects one extra newest-first item, which sliceLast(limit) drops again: same result (TS identical).

name: health-skip-malformed
find: if v, err := parseJSON([]byte(line)); err == nil {
replace: if v, err := parseJSON([]byte(line)); err != nil || true {
reason: parseJSON returns a nil value on error and accumulateCheckpointHealth(nil) returns at once: same result.

name: oracle-default-code
reason: unreachable: failedAttempts>=1 implies lastFailure with errorCode in {config,provider,aborted,invalid_output}; maxFailedAttemptsPerBlocker is >=1.

name: oracle-abort-keeps-active
reason: unreachable: the flow passes no abort signal to runBlockerOracle (the original neither), so errorCode 'aborted' never occurs.

name: task-reopen-skipped-only
find:
if gstr(task, "status") != "skipped" {
				return goalGate{message: fmt.Sprintf("Task \"%s\" is not skipped
replace:
if gstr(task, "status") == "pending" {
				return goalGate{message: fmt.Sprintf("Task \"%s\" is not skipped
reason: unreachable: record normalization maps any status except complete/skipped to pending, so the pending-only comparison is the same.

name: task-no-list
find:
if c.state().obj("taskList") == nil {
		return c.textResult("The goal has no task list.")
replace:
if false {
		return c.textResult("The goal has no task list.")
reason: duplicate guard: updateTask returns the identical message 'The goal has no task list.' for a goal without a task list.

name: complete-progress-lines
reason: the dashboard renderer shows at most 3 recentOutput lines (i >= 3 break), so a cap of 8 or 4 renders alike; c.auditProgress is cleared right after.

name: commit-focus-token
replace:
focusToken: func() *goalFocusToken { _ = token; return nil }(),
		mutate: func(*jsObject) *jsObject {
reason: the focus was re-checked (isFocusedOperationCurrent) on the line before the commit with no yield in between, so the token check in apply cannot fail.

name: events-sessionkey-swapped-model
reason: (provider,id)->(id,provider) is a bijection on the key; equal and distinct sessions compare the same.

name: events-budget-over-sign
reason: unreachable: budgetRemaining clamps at 0, so remaining<0 never holds.

name: events-start-settings-cache
reason: loadState (called by session_start) invalidates the settings cache itself (core.go), so the second invalidation is redundant.

name: events-start-select-no-arm
reason: session_start ends with beginAccounting and scheduler.restore, which repeat everything armFocusedContinuation does for the selected goal.

name: events-end-signal-no-return
reason: after pauseActiveGoal the goal is paused: the continuing statements only persist/refresh again and set a settle id that agent_settled finds not actionable.

name: events-settled-actionable
reason: scheduler.settled(true) on a goal that is no longer the run's active goal returns at its own status/runGoalID checks; both branches end in return nil.

name: events-settled-returns-late
reason: agent_end sets exactly one of the two settle ids, so with actionable true networkErrorGoalID is nil and the next statement returns anyway.

name: events-ledger-read-once-broken
reason: the ledger snapshot is only cached per hook (one local read); re-reading each time returns the same events: performance only.

name: events-archive-commit
reason: commitFocused true only re-focuses the archived goal, which archiveDeferredCompletion drops right after (goals.delete, assignFocused(nil)).

name: events-turn-start-wrong-goal
reason: the turn's goal id is reassigned to the focused goal at the turn's first mutation; if the focus moved before it, both branches rebuild the transaction from the focused goal and differ only in turnBase being the live goal versus a copy with the same usage values.

name: choose-complete-skip
reason: chooseOpenGoal is only called through chooseOpenGoalAwaited, which every caller guards with c.state()==nil after its own reconcile; the second reconcile in chooseOpenGoal cannot create a state, so `g != nil && status != complete` is never true

name: select-empty-label
reason: a picked "" never equals any label (goalSelectorLabel is never empty), so the label loop returns ("", false) exactly as the early return does

name: menu-header-skip
reason: a header row (starts with "───") that is not skipped falls through: "Editing: ..." has a colon but its label "─── Editing" matches no row, the others have no colon, so every path ends in `continue` as the skip does

name: menu-min-oracle
reason: the oracle rows carry a path and their keys (oracleMaxFailedAttemptsPerBlocker, ...) are never stallTimeoutMinutes/objectiveMaxChars/maxAutonomousRuns, so dropping `row.path == nil &&` leaves min at 1 for them either way

name: menu-local-override
find: if hasLocalOverride && prov != nil && prov.source == string(scope) {
reason: hasLocalOverride (project layer defines the path) implies resolveLeaf picks the project value, so provenance.source is "project" (env-only rows never reach this branch: envOverrideFor skips them); the source check is always true when the first operand is

name: status-focused
find: focused:           view != nil && c.focused != nil && *c.focused == gstr(view, "id"),
reason: view is c.goalForDisplay() or c.state(), both the goal c.focused points at, so `view != nil` already implies c.focused != nil and *c.focused == id

name: status-sync-prompt
reason: showGoalStatus reconciles first; after it the focused goal object is the pool cache object (or the disk goal), and mergeGoalPromptFromDisk takes the objective from that same cache, so syncGoalPromptFromDisk never changes the displayed objective

name: segments: tail guard
reason: tailStart -1 makes `tasksStart >= tailStart` true for any tasksStart >= 0 (and tasksStart < 0 returns nil), so nil is returned either way

name: fit: no budget returns head
reason: at budget 0 the fall-through computes out = head and appends rest[len(rest):], an empty slice: the same result as the early return

name: fitOptions: block guard
reason: the head keeps at least one line, so with optionsBlockLen == maxDialogLines the total is always >= block+1 > max and the function returns nil at the end anyway

name: task dialog: up wraps
reason: there are exactly two options, so (s-1+2)%2 == (s+1)%2 for both selections

name: svc-apply-midturn-pending-msg
find: msg = "Previous goal changes are still awaiting persistence."
reason: the default message is used only when flushTurn leaves the turn active with an empty flushError, but flushTurn only keeps a turn active after setting flushError (lock contention)

name: svc-ledger-batch-threshold
reason: appendGoalEvent(e) is appendLedgerLines([e]) and appendGoalEvents([e]) is the same call, so sending a single event through the batch call writes the same bytes

name: svc-task-attempt-merge-prompt
reason: after reconcileFocused the current goal is the pool cache object, and mergeGoalPromptFromDisk takes the objective from that cache (or the file the cache was read from), so the merged objective equals current

name: svc-sameTasks-empty
reason: two empty task slices: returning false only runs removeTasks/indexTasks on empty slices, which do nothing

name: ledger-completed-stub-status
reason: the stub status is overwritten by `st.latestStatus = "complete"` on the next line

name: ledger-cp-tail-gate
reason: the coveredBytes == size case returns on the line above, so `<` and `<=` select the same inputs

name: mutate-thinking-unset-alias
reason: mutateSettingsLayer builds the mutation target from the parsed layer, which only ever holds the normalized key "thinkingLevel" (the "thinking_level" spelling is renamed on parse), so the alias delete has nothing to delete

name: draft-flush-buffered
reason: flushForAudit leaves a turn buffered only through lock contention, which sets flushError; `isTurnBuffered() && flushError == ""` cannot hold

name: task dialog: width cap
reason: dialogInnerWidth(termWidth, 64) caps the width at 64 before use, so clamping the terminal width at 80 or 81 first changes nothing

name: svc-fresh-disk-no-activepath
reason: with an empty activePath resolveGoalPath(goalsDir, "") is the goals directory itself, which parseGoalFile cannot read as a goal: nil, as the early return gives

name: audit-session-suffix-only-custom
reason: pigCustomToolSuffix(nil) is the empty string, so appending it for zero custom tools changes nothing

name: audit-session-linewriter-flush-skip
reason: skip is only set together with buf=nil (Write) and cleared with it, so skip implies len(buf)==0 and the added guard is redundant

name: audit-proc-setpgid-2
reason: audit_proc_other_unix.go has the build tag unix && !linux and is not compiled on the Linux mutation host (the Setpgid test in mutants_d_unix_test.go covers it on darwin)

name: bound-le-cap
reason: with len(lines)==cap, lines[:cap] is the same slice content as lines; the < vs <= split returns identical output

name: escape-term-width
reason: the 80 cap is shadowed by dialogInnerWidth(termWidth, 64), which caps at 64 anyway: any cap >= 64 gives the same inner width

name: scaffold-max-inner
reason: termWidth > maxInner and termWidth >= maxInner+1 are the same predicate for integers

name: overlay-term-width
reason: the 100 cap is shadowed by dialogInnerWidth(termWidth, 90), which caps at 90: any cap >= 90 gives the same inner width (also in HandleInput)
